skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guide agents through root-cause debugging before proposing fixes, with focused investigation, hypothesis testing, and verification steps.
skill.summary: A structured debugging workflow for finding root causes before making code changes.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, ordinary NODE_ENV checks, and prose examples. remediation.issue: Diagnostic commands may reveal signing identity and environment metadata in logs.
remediation.suggestion: Replace env and keychain enumeration examples with redacted checks, and warn users not to print secrets or signing identities in shared logs.

remediation.issue: The helper script runs project tests and inspects user-selected paths.
remediation.suggestion: Document that find-polluter.sh should only be run in trusted repositories and that test commands may execute project code.

content.value_statement: Random fixes waste time and often create new defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence gathering, hypothesis testing, and verified fixes.
actual_capabilities: Provides a four-phase workflow for investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation.
Prompts agents to reproduce failures and gather evidence before proposing code changes.
Explains how to trace invalid data backward through a call chain to the original trigger.
Includes guidance for replacing arbitrary sleeps with condition-based waiting in tests.
Supplies a shell helper for finding which test creates unwanted files or state.
Defines red flags that indicate an agent is guessing instead of debugging.
limitations: It does not automatically inspect a repository or run commands without agent or user action.
It cannot guarantee a root cause when failures depend on external systems or missing evidence.
Some examples include shell commands that should be reviewed before use in sensitive environments.
The process may be slower than a temporary mitigation during an active production incident.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to reproduce failures, compare working examples, and test one hypothesis at a time.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Automation
use_cases.description: Replace arbitrary sleeps with condition-based waiting and identify the state that tests should observe.

use_cases.title: Guide Incident Debugging
use_cases.description: Structure evidence gathering during outages while separating immediate mitigation from root-cause repair.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bug Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic-debugging for this failure. First list the observed error, reproduction steps, recent changes, and missing evidence before suggesting any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the four debugging phases to this failing test. Identify the root-cause hypothesis, the smallest test for it, and the verification command.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Bad Data Backward
prompt_templates.prompt: Use root-cause tracing for this invalid value. Walk backward through callers, record where the value changes, and stop only at the original trigger.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Three attempted fixes failed. Use systematic-debugging to re-evaluate the architecture, list evidence for each failed hypothesis, and propose the next investigation step.

output_examples.input: A payment status test sometimes receives pending instead of completed.
output: The response should first document the exact failure and reproduction pattern.
It should identify missing evidence about the status transition and async boundary.
It should propose one hypothesis and one minimal verification step before any fix.

output_examples.input: A command created a .git directory in the source tree during tests.
output: The response should trace the directory value through each caller.
It should find where an empty or wrong path was introduced.
It should recommend fixing the source and adding validation at multiple layers.

output_examples.input: A flaky test uses several fixed sleep calls.
output: The response should name the condition the test actually needs.
It should replace sleeps with polling that has a timeout and clear error message.
It should keep true timing checks only when the timing behavior is the subject of the test.

best_practices: Gather reproducible evidence before proposing a code change.
Test one hypothesis with the smallest possible change.
Verify the final fix with the failing case and relevant regression tests.
anti_patterns: Adding a quick workaround before understanding the failure path.
Changing several variables at once and then guessing which one helped.
Treating repeated failed fixes as implementation trouble instead of a signal to re-analyze.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, failing tests, unexpected behavior, build failures, performance issues, and integration problems.

faq.question: Does it make the agent slower?
faq.answer: It adds investigation steps, but it reduces wasted time from repeated guesses and unstable fixes.

faq.question: Can it help during production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, but urgent mitigation may come first. Use the process to keep evidence and root-cause repair separate.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides process guidance and examples. Any command execution depends on the agent and user environment.

faq.question: What should I avoid with the included examples?
faq.answer: Do not print secrets, keychain data, or sensitive environment values into shared logs.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
